vi.L: Vậy hãy coi chừng các con nghe thế nào; vì ai có, sẽ được cho [thêm], còn ai không có, thì ngay cả điều người ấy dường như có cũng sẽ bị lấy đi."
vi.B: Vậy hãy chú ý cách các con lắng nghe. Ai có sẽ được cho thêm; còn ai không có thì ngay cả điều mình tưởng là có cũng sẽ bị lấy mất."
vi.R: Vậy hãy cẩn thận về cách các con lắng nghe! Ai đã có sẽ được cho thêm. Còn ai không có thì ngay cả điều mình nghĩ là mình có cũng sẽ bị lấy mất."

decisions.choice: whoever has: whoever has taken in the word and keeps it
decisions.reason: In this setting "having" is about the word that is heard. Those who hold it fast (8:15) gain more understanding; those who let it go lose even what they once heard.

decisions.choice: seems to have: appears to have, or thinks he has
decisions.reason: The verb can mean "seem" or "think". What such a hearer has is only an appearance.

decisions.choice: will be given, will be taken away: by God
decisions.reason: The passives leave God as the one who gives and takes away.

decisions.choice: those who have; those who do not have
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural, which speaks of anyone without needing a singular pronoun.

decisions.choice: what they think they have
decisions.reason: Readable takes the other sense of the verb, which is easier to follow and comes to the same thing.

decisions.choice: "가졌다고 생각하는 것" (L, R); "가진 줄로 여기는 것" (B) for "what he seems to have"
decisions.reason: The verb can mean "seems" or "thinks" (meaning decision); Korean "생각하다" and "여기다" hold both the person's own view and the appearance better than "보이다", which names only the outward look.

decisions.choice: "dường như có" (L); "tưởng là có" (B); "nghĩ là mình có" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision allows both "appears to have" and "thinks he has": Literal keeps the appearance with "dường như", Balanced and Readable say what the person supposes, as the English Readable does. No gender span: "ai" and "người ấy" are inclusive.

source.text: Παρεγένετο δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ μήτηρ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐκ ἠδύναντο συντυχεῖν αὐτῷ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον.

records.literal_gloss: Came then to him the mother and the brothers of him, and not they were able to reach him because of the crowd.

en.L: Then {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother and brothers came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they were not able to get to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} because of the crowd.
en.B: His mother and his brothers came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but the crowd kept them from getting to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: The mother and brothers of Jesus came to see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But there were so many people that they could not get close to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y vinieron a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hermanos, y no podían llegar hasta {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a causa de la multitud.
es.B: Su madre y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hermanos vinieron adonde {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estaba, pero la multitud les impedía acercarse a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: La madre y los hermanos de Jesús vinieron a verlo. Pero había tanta gente que no podían acercarse a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Alors {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} frères vinrent auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et ils ne pouvaient pas {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}approcher à cause de la foule.
fr.B: Sa mère et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} frères vinrent {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} trouver, mais la foule les empêchait d’arriver jusqu’à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: La mère et les frères de Jésus sont venus pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voir. Mais il y avait tellement de monde qu’ils ne pouvaient pas s’approcher de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Kisha mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} walikuja {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, nao hawakuweza kumfikia kwa sababu ya umati.
sw.B: Mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} walikuja {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, lakini umati uliwazuia wasimfikie.
sw.R: Mama na ndugu za Yesu walikuja kumwona. Lakini watu walikuwa wengi mno, hata hawakuweza kumkaribia.

ko.L: 그런데 그분의 어머니와 형제들이 그분께 왔으나, 무리 때문에 그분께 가까이 갈 수 없었다.
ko.B: 예수의 어머니와 형제들이 예수를 찾아왔으나, 무리 때문에 가까이 갈 수 없었다.
ko.R: 예수의 어머니와 형제들이 예수를 만나러 왔다. 그러나 사람들이 너무 많아서 가까이 갈 수가 없었다.

vi.L: Bấy giờ mẹ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và anh em {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nhưng không thể đến gần {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vì đoàn dân.
vi.B: Mẹ và các anh em của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến tìm {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nhưng vì đám đông nên không đến gần {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được.
vi.R: Mẹ và các anh em của Đức Giê-xu đến gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Nhưng người ta đông quá, nên họ không đến gần {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được.

decisions.choice: brothers: Jesus's brothers in his family
decisions.reason: The word normally means brothers. Mark 6:3 names four of them and mentions sisters. Some Christian traditions understand them as relatives or as sons of Joseph by an earlier marriage; the text itself does not say.

decisions.choice: came to see him; there were so many people
alternatives: came to him; because of the crowd
decisions.reason: Readable says why they came, from 8:20, and why the crowd stopped them.

decisions.choice: "형제들", not "동생들"; no gender span, as in Mark 3:31
decisions.reason: "동생들" would decide that they were younger brothers, which the text does not say; specific men of his family are meant (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "anh em" for his brothers
decisions.reason: As in Mark 3:31: "anh em" names brothers without saying whether they were older or younger, which the Greek does not say.

source.text: ἀπηγγέλη δὲ αὐτῷ· Ἡ μήτηρ σου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί σου ἑστήκασιν ἔξω ἰδεῖν σε θέλοντές.

records.literal_gloss: It was reported then to him: The mother of you and the brothers of you are standing outside to see you wanting.

en.L: And it was reported to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Your mother and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} brothers are standing outside, wanting to see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.B: Someone told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Your mother and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} brothers are standing outside, and they want to see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.R: Someone told Jesus, "Your mother and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} brothers are outside. They want to see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

es.L: Y se {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} anunció: «Tu madre y {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} hermanos están de pie afuera, queriendo verte».
es.B: Alguien {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} avisó: «Tu madre y {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} hermanos están afuera y quieren verte».
es.R: Alguien le dijo a Jesús: «Tu madre y {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} hermanos están afuera. Quieren verte».

fr.L: Et on {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} annonça : « Ta mère et {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} frères se tiennent dehors et veulent {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} voir. »
fr.B: Quelqu’un {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Ta mère et {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} frères sont dehors, et ils veulent {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} voir. »
fr.R: Quelqu’un a dit à Jésus : « Ta mère et {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} frères sont dehors. Ils veulent {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} voir. »

sw.L: Naye akaambiwa, "Mama {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} wamesimama nje, wakitaka kukuona."
sw.B: Mtu mmoja alimwambia, "Mama {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} wako nje, nao wanataka kukuona."
sw.R: Mtu fulani alimwambia Yesu, "Mama {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} wako nje. Wanataka kukuona."

ko.L: 그러자 그분께 [이런] 말이 전해졌다. "선생님의 어머니와 선생님의 형제들이 선생님을 보려고 밖에 서 계십니다."
ko.B: 어떤 사람이 예수께 알려 드렸다. "선생님의 어머니와 형제들이 선생님을 만나려고 밖에 서 계십니다."
ko.R: 누군가가 예수께 말했다. "선생님의 어머니와 형제들이 밖에 와 계십니다. 선생님을 만나고 싶어 하십니다."

vi.L: Và [có người] báo cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Mẹ Thầy và anh em Thầy đang đứng bên ngoài, muốn gặp Thầy."
vi.B: Có người báo cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Thầy, mẹ và anh em Thầy đang đứng ngoài kia, muốn gặp Thầy."
vi.R: Có người nói với Đức Giê-xu: "Thưa Thầy, mẹ và các anh em của Thầy đang ở ngoài. Họ muốn gặp Thầy."

decisions.choice: it was reported: someone told him
decisions.reason: The passive does not say who brought the message.

decisions.choice: Someone told
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply a subject so that the sentence can be active.

decisions.choice: verte, with no span
alternatives: te quieren ver, with a span on "te"
decisions.reason: The English "you" takes the setting. Spanish joins the pronoun to the infinitive ("verte"), and a joined pronoun takes no span, as the term sheet settles; the free possessive "tus" carries the setting instead.

decisions.choice: The speaker addresses Jesus in 합쇼체 and says "선생님" for "you"; "서 계십니다" honours his mother
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Mark 3:32, Korean does not address a respected teacher as "you", so "선생님" stands for the pronoun and Literal does not bracket it.

decisions.choice: "Thầy" for "you" and "your", with no setting span; "Thưa Thầy" added (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in the parallel Mark 3:32: the people around him speak to him as their teacher. "Thầy" is a noun of address and takes no span; a Vietnamese message to a teacher opens with "Thưa Thầy".

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Μήτηρ μου καὶ ἀδελφοί μου οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ ἀκούοντες καὶ ποιοῦντες.

records.literal_gloss: But answering he said to them: Mother of me and brothers of me these are those the word of God hearing and doing.

en.L: But answering, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "My mother and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brothers are these: those who hear the word of God and do [it]."
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered them, "Those who hear the word of God and do what it says are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mother and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brothers."
en.R: Jesus answered them, "People who hear the word of God and obey it are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mother and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brothers."

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, respondiendo, les dijo: «Mi madre y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} hermanos son estos: los que oyen la palabra de Dios y [la] hacen».
es.B: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les respondió: «Los que oyen la palabra de Dios y la ponen en práctica son {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} madre y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} hermanos».
es.R: Jesús les respondió: «Las personas que oyen la palabra de Dios y la obedecen son {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} madre y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} hermanos».

fr.L: Mais, répondant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Ma mère et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} frères, ce sont ceux qui entendent la parole de Dieu et [la] mettent en pratique. »
fr.B: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur répondit : « Ceux qui écoutent la parole de Dieu et la mettent en pratique, voilà {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} mère et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} frères. »
fr.R: Jésus leur a répondu : « Les gens qui écoutent la parole de Dieu et qui lui obéissent, ce sont eux, {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} mère et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} frères. »

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, akijibu, aliwaambia, "Mama {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} ni hawa: wale wanaolisikia neno la Mungu na kulitenda."
sw.B: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliwajibu, "Wale wanaolisikia neno la Mungu na kulitenda ndio mama {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}."
sw.R: Yesu aliwajibu, "Watu wanaolisikia neno la Mungu na kulitii ndio mama {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}."

ko.L: 그러나 그분이 그들에게 대답하여 말씀하셨다. "내 어머니와 내 형제들은 하나님의 말씀을 듣고 행하는 이 사람들이다."
ko.B: 그러나 예수께서 그들에게 대답하셨다. "하나님의 말씀을 듣고 그대로 행하는 사람들이 내 어머니이고 내 형제들이다."
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 대답하셨다. "하나님의 말씀을 듣고 그 말씀대로 사는 사람들이 바로 내 어머니이고 내 형제들이다."

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trả lời và nói với họ: "Mẹ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và anh em {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là những người này: những người nghe lời Đức Chúa Trời và làm theo."
vi.B: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đáp: "Những người nghe lời Đức Chúa Trời và làm theo, đó là mẹ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và anh em {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời họ: "Những người nghe lời Đức Chúa Trời và vâng theo lời ấy, chính họ là mẹ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và anh em {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."

decisions.choice: my mother and my brothers: all who hear and do God's word belong to Jesus's family
alternatives: a rejection of his own family
decisions.reason: Jesus does not turn his family away. His mother is herself one who heard God's word and trusted it (1:38, 45), and his mother and brothers are among the believers in Acts 1:14. He names a family that is wider than his relatives.

decisions.choice: hear and do: the good soil (8:15) and the house on rock (6:47)
decisions.reason: Jesus repeats the point of the parable and of the end of his sermon: hearing is not enough without doing.

decisions.choice: brothers: here, those who are family to Jesus, women as well as men
decisions.reason: The word answers the message about his brothers (8:20), but the people Jesus describes include women such as those who traveled with him (8:2-3).

decisions.choice: the people first, then my mother and my brothers
alternatives: My mother and my brothers are those who hear
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the surprising answer, Jesus's family, at the end of the sentence, where it stands out.

decisions.choice: brothers, with no inclusive setting
decisions.reason: Jesus takes up the word that was just used of his own brothers (8:20); "brothers and sisters" would hide that echo. The meaning decision notes that women are included.

decisions.choice: hermanos, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: Jesus's family here includes women as well as men (meaning decision m3), and the English keeps "brothers" with no setting. Spanish "hermanos" already includes sisters, as the term sheet notes, so it stays plain.

decisions.choice: ndugu, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: Jesus's family here includes women as well as men (meaning decision m3). Swahili "ndugu" already means brothers and sisters alike, so there is nothing for a setting to change.

decisions.choice: "형제들" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The saying sets Jesus's family beside those who hear and do God's word; Korean keeps "형제들" as the English keeps "brothers" without a setting, so the link with 8:19-20 stays visible. Korean "형제" in this saying is not limited to men.

decisions.choice: "anh em" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English keeps "brothers" with no setting, so the saying answers the words of 8:19-20; Vietnamese keeps the same "anh em" for the same reason. The meaning decision says women are included.

source.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν καὶ αὐτὸς ἐνέβη εἰς πλοῖον καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Διέλθωμεν εἰς τὸ πέραν τῆς λίμνης, καὶ ἀνήχθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: It came about then on one of the days that he got into a boat and the disciples of him, and he said to them: Let us go over to the other side of the lake; and they set out.

en.L: And it happened on one of the days that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into a boat, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Let us go over to the other side of the lake," and they set out.
en.B: One day Jesus got into a boat with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and said to them, "Let us cross over to the far side of the lake." So they put out from shore.
en.R: One day Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples got into a boat. He said to them, "Let us go across the lake to the other side." So they started out.

es.L: Y sucedió uno de los días que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} subió a una barca, y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, y les dijo: «Pasemos al otro lado del lago». Y zarparon.
es.B: Un día Jesús subió a una barca con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos y les dijo: «Crucemos a la otra orilla del lago». Así que zarparon.
es.R: Un día Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos subieron a una barca. Él les dijo: «Vamos a cruzar al otro lado del lago». Y salieron.

fr.L: Et il arriva, un de ces jours, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} monta dans une barque, ainsi que {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Passons de l’autre côté du lac. » Et ils prirent le large.
fr.B: Un jour, Jésus monta dans une barque avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples et leur dit : « Passons sur l’autre rive du lac. » Ils quittèrent donc le rivage.
fr.R: Un jour, Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples sont montés dans un bateau. Il leur a dit : « Allons de l’autre côté du lac. » Alors ils sont partis.

sw.L: Na ikawa siku moja {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliingia katika mashua, na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akawaambia, "Na tuvuke twende ng'ambo ya ziwa," nao wakaondoka.
sw.B: Siku moja Yesu aliingia katika mashua pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akawaambia, "Tuvuke twende ng'ambo ya ziwa." Basi wakaanza safari.
sw.R: Siku moja Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} waliingia katika mashua. Aliwaambia, "Twendeni upande wa pili wa ziwa." Basi wakaondoka.

ko.L: 그리고 어느 날 이런 일이 있었다. 그분과 그분의 제자들이 배에 올랐는데, 그분이 그들에게 "호수 건너편으로 건너가자" 하고 말씀하셨다. 그래서 그들이 배를 띄웠다.
ko.B: 어느 날 예수께서 제자들과 함께 배에 오르셔서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "호수 건너편으로 건너가자." 그래서 그들은 배를 띄워 떠났다.
ko.R: 어느 날 예수께서 제자들과 함께 배에 타셨다. 예수께서 제자들에게 말씀하셨다. "호수 건너편으로 가자." 그래서 그들은 떠났다.

vi.L: Và xảy ra vào một trong những ngày ấy, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bước xuống thuyền cùng các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Chúng ta hãy qua bờ bên kia hồ." Và họ ra khơi.
vi.B: Một hôm, Đức Giê-xu xuống thuyền với các môn đồ và nói với họ: "Chúng ta hãy qua bờ hồ bên kia." Vậy họ rời bờ.
vi.R: Một ngày kia, Đức Giê-xu và các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lên một chiếc thuyền. Ngài nói với họ: "Chúng ta hãy đi qua bên kia hồ." Vậy họ lên đường.

decisions.choice: the lake: the Lake of Galilee, also called Gennesaret
decisions.reason: Luke calls it a lake (5:1). It is about 13 miles long. The other side is the eastern shore, where many Gentiles lived (8:26).

decisions.choice: they set out: they put out from land
alternatives: they set sail on a long voyage
decisions.reason: The verb is a sailing word for putting a boat out from shore.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: el lago (every level)
decisions.reason: Luke calls the Sea of Galilee a lake, using the Greek word for a lake (meaning decision m1), so "lago" stands at every level, Literal included, unlike Mark's "mar". The same in verses 23 and 33.

decisions.choice: une barque (L, B), un bateau (R); le lac at every level
decisions.reason: As in Mark 4-5: "barque" is the usual French word for a small fishing boat, and Readable uses the everyday "bateau". Luke calls the Sea of Galilee a lake (m1), so French says "le lac" at every level, Literal included.

decisions.choice: ziwa (every level)
decisions.reason: Luke calls the Sea of Galilee a lake, using the Greek word for a lake (meaning decision m1), so "ziwa" stands at every level, Literal included, unlike Mark's "bahari". The same in verses 23 and 33.

decisions.choice: "호수" at every level for Luke's limnē (8:22-33), as at Luke 5:1
decisions.reason: Mark says "sea" and the Korean Mark keeps "바다" at Literal and Balanced; Luke chooses the word for a lake, so every level says "호수".

decisions.choice: "hồ" at every level (whole chapter)
decisions.reason: Luke's word means a lake, as at 5:1 (the Lake of Gennesaret), where Mark says "sea" ("biển" at Literal and Balanced in Mark 4-5); Vietnamese follows Luke's word at every level.

source.text: πλεόντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἀφύπνωσεν.

records.literal_gloss: Sailing then [of] them, he fell asleep.

en.L: And as they were sailing, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} fell asleep.
en.B: While they were sailing, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} fell asleep.
en.R: While they were sailing, Jesus fell asleep.

es.L: Y mientras navegaban, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se quedó dormido.
es.B: Mientras navegaban, se durmió.
es.R: Mientras navegaban, Jesús se quedó dormido.

fr.L: Et pendant qu’ils naviguaient, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’endormit.
fr.B: Pendant la traversée, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’endormit.
fr.R: Pendant qu’ils naviguaient, Jésus s’est endormi.

sw.L: Na walipokuwa wakisafiri, alilala usingizi.
sw.B: Walipokuwa wakisafiri, alipitiwa na usingizi.
sw.R: Walipokuwa wakisafiri, Yesu alilala usingizi.

ko.L: 그런데 그들이 배를 저어 가는 동안 그분은 잠이 드셨다.
ko.B: 배를 타고 가는 동안 예수께서는 잠이 드셨다.
ko.R: 배를 타고 가는 동안 예수께서는 잠이 드셨다.

vi.L: Và trong khi họ đang đi thuyền, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngủ thiếp đi.
vi.B: Trong lúc thuyền đang đi, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngủ thiếp đi.
vi.R: Trong khi họ đi thuyền, Đức Giê-xu ngủ thiếp đi.

decisions.choice: fell asleep: dropped off to sleep
decisions.reason: The verb describes falling asleep during the voyage. Jesus was tired, as any person would be after a day of teaching.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus, since the disciples were the last people mentioned.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun span only on the separate pronoun: él (L); none at Balanced
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out ("se durmió"), so there is nothing separate to capitalise; Literal keeps "él", as the Greek names him. The setting therefore covers fewer words than in English, throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on alilala, alipitiwa (he fell asleep)
decisions.reason: The English "he" takes the setting. Swahili carries it in the subject prefix a- of the verb, which cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives (yeye, naye, wake). Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English throughout the chapter.

source.text: καὶ κατέβη λαῖλαψ ἀνέμου εἰς τὴν λίμνην, καὶ συνεπληροῦντο καὶ ἐκινδύνευον.

records.literal_gloss: And came down a storm of wind onto the lake, and they were being filled up and were in danger.

en.L: And a storm of wind came down onto the lake, and they were being filled [with water] and were in danger.
en.B: A fierce windstorm swept down on the lake. Water was filling the boat, and they were in danger.
en.R: A strong windstorm came down on the lake. Waves began to fill the boat with water, and they were in danger of sinking.

es.L: Y bajó una tempestad de viento sobre el lago, y se iban llenando [de agua] y estaban en peligro.
es.B: Una violenta tormenta de viento se abatió sobre el lago. La barca se iba llenando de agua, y estaban en peligro.
es.R: Un viento muy fuerte bajó sobre el lago. Las olas empezaron a llenar de agua la barca, y estaban en peligro de hundirse.

fr.L: Et une tempête de vent descendit sur le lac, et ils se remplissaient [d’eau] et étaient en danger.
fr.B: Une violente bourrasque s’abattit sur le lac ; la barque se remplissait d’eau, et ils étaient en danger.
fr.R: Un vent très fort s’est abattu sur le lac. Les vagues ont commencé à remplir le bateau d’eau, et ils risquaient de couler.

sw.L: Na dhoruba ya upepo ikashuka juu ya ziwa, nao walikuwa wakijazwa [maji] na kuwa hatarini.
sw.B: Dhoruba kali ya upepo ilishuka juu ya ziwa. Mashua ikawa inajaa maji, nao wakawa hatarini.
sw.R: Upepo mkali sana ulishuka juu ya ziwa. Mawimbi yakaanza kuijaza mashua maji, nao walikuwa katika hatari ya kuzama.

ko.L: 그리고 호수에 거센 바람이 내리 불어서, 그들은 [물이] 차올라 위험에 빠졌다.
ko.B: 그때 거센 돌풍이 호수로 내리 불어서, 배에 물이 차고 그들은 위험에 빠졌다.
ko.R: 그때 아주 센 바람이 호수로 불어 닥쳤다. 큰 물결이 배 안으로 들이쳐서 배에 물이 찼다. 그들은 물에 빠져 죽을 위험에 놓였다.

vi.L: Và một trận bão gió ập xuống trên hồ, và họ bị nước tràn đầy, và đang lâm nguy.
vi.B: Một trận bão lớn ập xuống mặt hồ. Nước tràn vào thuyền, và họ gặp nguy hiểm.
vi.R: Một trận gió bão rất mạnh thổi xuống mặt hồ. Sóng làm nước tràn vào thuyền, và họ sắp bị chìm.

decisions.choice: came down: a sudden storm rushing down onto the lake
alternatives: a storm that built up slowly
decisions.reason: The lake lies low among hills, and winds can sweep down on it suddenly and stir up dangerous waves.

decisions.choice: they were being filled: the boat was filling with water, with them in it
alternatives: the disciples were being filled with fear
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the people, but what was filling was the boat. Mark 4:37 says the waves were breaking into the boat.

decisions.choice: the boat; of sinking (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was filling, as the meaning decision explains, and Readable says what the danger was.

decisions.choice: "[물이] 차올라" (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek says only that they were being filled; Korean needs to say with what, so Literal brackets it (meaning decision: the boat was filling with water).

source.text: προσελθόντες δὲ διήγειραν αὐτὸν λέγοντες· Ἐπιστάτα ἐπιστάτα, ἀπολλύμεθα· ὁ δὲ διεγερθεὶς ἐπετίμησεν τῷ ἀνέμῳ καὶ τῷ κλύδωνι τοῦ ὕδατος, καὶ ἐπαύσαντο, καὶ ἐγένετο γαλήνη.

records.literal_gloss: Having come then they woke him, saying: Master, master, we are perishing! And he, having been awoken, rebuked the wind and the rough water of the water, and they ceased, and there was a calm.

en.L: And they came and woke {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Master, Master, we are perishing!" And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, having woken up, rebuked the wind and the rough waves of the water, and they ceased, and there was a calm.
en.B: They went and roused {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, crying out, "Master, Master, we are lost!" He stood up and gave a stern order to the wind and the churning water. They stopped, and the lake became calm.
en.R: The disciples went to Jesus and woke {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up. They said, "Master! Master! We are going to die!" Jesus got up. He gave orders to the wind and the big waves. They stopped, and everything was calm.

es.L: Y acercándose, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} despertaron, diciendo: «¡Maestro, Maestro, perecemos!». Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, despertándose, increpó al viento y al oleaje del agua, y cesaron, y se hizo la calma.
es.B: Se acercaron a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} despertaron, gritando: «¡Maestro, Maestro, nos hundimos!». Él se levantó y dio una orden firme al viento y al agua agitada. Cesaron, y todo quedó en calma.
es.R: Los discípulos fueron adonde estaba Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} despertaron. Le dijeron: «¡Maestro! ¡Maestro! ¡Nos vamos a morir!». Jesús se levantó. Dio órdenes al viento y a las grandes olas. Se detuvieron, y todo quedó tranquilo.

fr.L: Et, s’étant approchés, ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} réveillèrent, disant : « Maître, Maître, nous périssons ! » Et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, s’étant réveillé, reprit sévèrement le vent et les flots agités de l’eau ; et ils cessèrent, et il se fit un calme.
fr.B: Ils allèrent {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} réveiller en criant : « Maître, Maître, nous sommes perdus ! » Jésus se leva et donna un ordre sévère au vent et aux flots déchaînés. Ils s’apaisèrent, et le lac redevint calme.
fr.R: Les disciples sont allés réveiller Jésus. Ils ont crié : « Maître ! Maître ! Nous allons mourir ! » Jésus s’est levé. Il a donné des ordres au vent et aux grosses vagues. Le vent et les vagues se sont calmés, et tout est redevenu tranquille.

sw.L: Nao wakimkaribia walimwamsha, wakisema, "Mkuu, Mkuu, tunaangamia!" Naye, akiisha kuamka, aliukemea upepo na mawimbi makali ya maji, navyo vikakoma, kukawa shwari.
sw.B: Walimwendea, wakamwamsha, wakilia, "Mkuu, Mkuu, tumekwisha!" Yeye akaamka, akatoa amri kali kwa upepo na kwa maji yaliyochafuka. Vikatulia, na ziwa likawa shwari.
sw.R: Wanafunzi walimwendea Yesu, wakamwamsha. Walisema, "Mkuu! Mkuu! Tutakufa!" Yesu aliamka. Akauamuru upepo na mawimbi makubwa. Vikatulia, na kila kitu kikawa shwari.

ko.L: 그러자 그들이 다가가서 그분을 깨우며 말했다. "선생님, 선생님, 저희가 죽게 되었습니다!" 그분이 깨어나셔서 바람과 거친 물결을 꾸짖으시니, 그것들이 그치고 잔잔해졌다.
ko.B: 제자들이 다가가서 예수를 깨우며 소리쳤다. "선생님, 선생님, 저희가 다 죽게 되었습니다!" 예수께서 일어나셔서 바람과 사나운 물결을 꾸짖으셨다. 그러자 바람과 물결이 그치고 호수가 잔잔해졌다.
ko.R: 제자들이 예수께 가서 예수를 깨웠다. 그들이 말했다. "선생님! 선생님! 저희가 다 죽게 생겼습니다!" 예수께서 일어나셔서 바람과 큰 물결에게 엄하게 명령하셨다. 그러자 바람과 물결이 멈추고, 모든 것이 잔잔해졌다.

vi.L: Họ đến đánh thức {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nói: "Thưa Thầy, thưa Thầy, chúng con đang chết!" Còn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, khi thức dậy, quở gió và sóng nước dữ dội; và chúng ngừng lại, và trở nên yên lặng.
vi.B: Họ đến đánh thức {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và kêu lên: "Thưa Thầy, thưa Thầy, chúng con chết mất!" Ngài thức dậy, quở gió và sóng nước cuồn cuộn. Gió và sóng ngừng lại, và mặt hồ trở nên yên lặng.
vi.R: Các môn đồ đến đánh thức Đức Giê-xu. Họ nói: "Thưa Thầy! Thưa Thầy! Chúng con sắp chết rồi!" Đức Giê-xu thức dậy. Ngài ra lệnh cho gió và những đợt sóng lớn. Gió và sóng ngừng lại, và mọi sự trở nên yên lặng.

decisions.choice: Master: one who has authority and gives orders
decisions.reason: This is the disciples' word for Jesus in Luke (5:5; 8:45; 9:33). They say it twice in their alarm.

decisions.choice: we are perishing: we are about to be destroyed, we are going to die
decisions.reason: The verb means to be destroyed or to die. They expect to drown.

decisions.choice: rebuked: commanded sternly, with authority
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the wind as he spoke to the demon (4:35) and the fever (4:39).

decisions.choice: the wind and waves obey: Scripture says that God stills the sea
decisions.reason: The Psalms praise the LORD, who rules the raging sea and stills its waves (Psalm 89:10; 107:29). Jesus does what Scripture says God does, which leads to the question in 8:25.

decisions.choice: we are lost (B); We are going to die (R)
decisions.reason: "Perishing" sounds bookish in a cry for help. Balanced and Readable use words people would shout in danger.

decisions.choice: the churning water (B); the big waves (R)
decisions.reason: The word means rough, surging water.

decisions.choice: Maestro (every level)
decisions.reason: Luke's word is a title for one in charge who gives orders (meaning decision m1), which the English renders "Master" against "Teacher" for the usual word (verse 49). Spanish has no common respectful address that matches it: "Jefe" is too casual for public reading and "Señor" is kept for "Lord" and "sir". So "Maestro" serves for both, and the difference is lost; the same in verse 45.

decisions.choice: Maître
decisions.reason: "Maître" is the French form of address for one who has authority over his followers (m1), as in Mark 4:38. "Chef" and "Patron" are not used to address someone in this register. French also uses "le maître" for the Teacher in 8:49, as Mark 5:35 does, so the two Greek words meet in one French word there.

decisions.choice: Mkuu (every level)
decisions.reason: Luke's word is a title for one in charge who gives orders (meaning decision m1), which the English renders "Master" against "Teacher" for the usual word (verse 49). "Mkuu" is the respectful address to a person in charge, and keeps "Mwalimu" for "Teacher"; the same in verse 45.

decisions.choice: "선생님" for epistata; the disciples speak in 합쇼체 and call themselves "저희"
decisions.reason: As settled at Luke 5:5 and in the parallel Mark 4:38.

decisions.choice: "꾸짖다" (L, B); "엄하게 명령하다" (R) for epitimaō
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the verb Luke uses for the demons and the fever (4:35, 4:39), as in Mark 4:39; Readable says what it means (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "Thưa Thầy" for Luke's "Master", and "chúng con" for the disciples
decisions.reason: As in Luke 5:5: Luke's word is for one in charge who gives orders (meaning decision), and Vietnamese has no closer respectful address than "Thưa Thầy"; the disciples call themselves "chúng con" as in Mark 4:38.

decisions.choice: "quở" (L, B); "ra lệnh" (R) for rebuked
decisions.reason: As in Mark 4:39 and Matthew 8:26: "quở" is the word for a stern rebuke with authority (meaning decision); Readable uses the everyday "ra lệnh".

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτοῖς· Ποῦ ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν;

records.literal_gloss: He said then to them: Where [is] the faith of you?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Where [is] your faith?"
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "Where is your faith?"
en.R: Then Jesus asked them, "Where is your faith?"

es.L: Y les dijo: «¿Dónde [está] {{plural_you:la fe de ustedes|vuestra fe}}?».
es.B: Entonces les preguntó: «¿Dónde está {{plural_you:la fe de ustedes|vuestra fe}}?».
es.R: Entonces Jesús les preguntó: «¿Dónde está {{plural_you:la fe de ustedes|vuestra fe}}?».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Où [est] votre foi ? »
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur demanda : « Où est votre foi ? »
fr.R: Puis Jésus leur a demandé : « Où est votre foi ? »

sw.L: Akawaambia, "Imani yenu [iko] wapi?"
sw.B: Kisha aliwauliza, "Imani yenu iko wapi?"
sw.R: Kisha Yesu aliwauliza, "Imani yenu iko wapi?"

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "너희의 믿음이 어디 있느냐?"
ko.B: 그리고 예수께서 그들에게 물으셨다. "너희의 믿음이 어디 있느냐?"
ko.R: 그리고 예수께서 그들에게 물으셨다. "너희 믿음이 어디 있느냐?"

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Đức tin của các con ở đâu?"
vi.B: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hỏi họ: "Đức tin của các con đâu rồi?"
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu hỏi họ: "Đức tin của các con ở đâu?"

decisions.choice: faith: trust in God and in Jesus's power
decisions.reason: The question suggests that they had faith but did not use it when danger came. Mark 4:40 has a sharper question, "Do you still have no faith?"

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

decisions.choice: "믿음" at every level
decisions.reason: Faith is a key term and keeps one Korean word at every level, as in Mark 4:40.

source.text: φοβηθέντες δὲ ἐθαύμασαν, λέγοντες πρὸς ἀλλήλους· Τίς ἄρα οὗτός ἐστιν ὅτι καὶ τοῖς ἀνέμοις ἐπιτάσσει καὶ τῷ ὕδατι, καὶ ὑπακούουσιν αὐτῷ;

records.literal_gloss: Having been afraid then they marveled, saying to one another: Who then this is, that even the winds he commands and the water, and they obey him?

en.L: And being afraid, they marveled, saying to one another, "Who then is this, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commands even the winds and the water, and they obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?"
en.B: Filled with fear and wonder, they asked one another, "Who is this, then, that the winds and the water obey when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives the order?"
en.R: The disciples were afraid and amazed. They asked each other, "Who is this man? He gives orders to the wind and the water, and they obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

es.L: Y, teniendo miedo, se maravillaron, diciéndose unos a otros: «¿Quién, pues, es este, que manda aun a los vientos y al agua, y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} obedecen?».
es.B: Llenos de temor y asombro, se preguntaban unos a otros: «¿Quién es este, entonces, que hasta los vientos y el agua obedecen cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} da la orden?».
es.R: Los discípulos tenían miedo y estaban asombrados. Se preguntaban unos a otros: «¿Quién es este hombre? ¡Da órdenes al viento y al agua, y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} obedecen!».

fr.L: Et, saisis de crainte, ils s’étonnèrent, se disant les uns aux autres : « Qui donc est celui-ci, pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} commande même aux vents et à l’eau, et qu’ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} obéissent ? »
fr.B: Remplis de crainte et d’étonnement, ils se demandaient les uns aux autres : « Qui est-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donc, pour que les vents et l’eau {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} obéissent quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donne un ordre ? »
fr.R: Les disciples avaient peur et ils étaient étonnés. Ils se sont demandé les uns aux autres : « Qui est cet homme ? Il donne des ordres au vent et à l’eau, et ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} obéissent ! »

sw.L: Nao, wakiwa na hofu, walistaajabu, wakisemezana, "Basi huyu ni nani, hata anauamuru upepo na maji, navyo vinamtii?"
sw.B: Wakiwa wamejaa hofu na mshangao, waliulizana, "Basi huyu ni nani, ambaye upepo na maji vinamtii anapotoa amri?"
sw.R: Wanafunzi waliogopa na kushangaa. Waliulizana, "Mtu huyu ni nani? Anatoa amri kwa upepo na maji, navyo vinamtii!"

ko.L: 그들은 두려워하며 놀라서 서로 말했다. "그러면 이분이 누구이시기에 바람과 물에게까지 명령하시고, 그것들이 이분에게 순종하는가?"
ko.B: 그들은 두려워하면서도 놀라워하며 서로 말했다. "도대체 이분이 누구이시기에 바람과 물에게 명령하시니, 그것들이 순종하는가?"
ko.R: 제자들은 무서우면서도 놀라웠다. 그들은 서로 말했다. "이분은 도대체 어떤 분이신가? 이분이 바람과 물에게 명령하시니, 바람과 물이 이분의 말씀을 듣는구나!"

vi.L: Và họ sợ hãi và kinh ngạc, nói với nhau: "Vậy người này là ai, mà truyền lệnh cả cho gió và nước, và chúng vâng lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}?"
vi.B: Họ vừa sợ hãi vừa kinh ngạc, hỏi nhau: "Vậy người này là ai mà khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} truyền lệnh thì cả gió lẫn nước đều vâng theo?"
vi.R: Các môn đồ vừa sợ vừa ngạc nhiên. Họ hỏi nhau: "Người này là ai vậy? Ngài ra lệnh cho gió và nước, và chúng vâng lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}!"

decisions.choice: who then is this: the question the whole story raises
decisions.reason: In Scripture it is God who commands the wind and the sea (Psalm 107:25-29). Luke lets the question stand; Peter answers it in 9:20.

decisions.choice: being afraid: awe at power beyond any human
decisions.reason: The storm is over. Now they fear the one who stopped it, as Simon did after the great catch of fish (5:8-10).

decisions.choice: this man
decisions.reason: Readable supplies "man", as the disciples are asking about a person.

decisions.choice: upepo for the plural "winds"
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering: "upepo" serves for wind and winds, since the plural "pepo" is also the word for demons, who appear in the next story.

decisions.choice: The disciples speak among themselves in the plain style (-는가) but of Jesus with the honorific ("이분", "누구이시기에")
decisions.reason: As in Mark 4:41 in Korean: equals speak to one another in 해라체, but awe, not hostility, is the point of the question, so they speak of their teacher with respect.

decisions.choice: "người này" for "this one"; "Ngài" for "he" and "him"
decisions.reason: As in Mark 4:41: "người này" keeps the open question, and the pronouns that follow are the reverent "Ngài" under the setting, since the question points to who he is.

source.text: Καὶ κατέπλευσαν εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν Γερασηνῶν, ἥτις ἐστὶν ἀντιπέρα τῆς Γαλιλαίας.

records.literal_gloss: And they sailed down to the region of the Gerasenes, which is opposite Galilee.

en.L: And they sailed down to the region of the Gerasenes, which is opposite Galilee.
en.B: They put in at the land of the Gerasenes, on the shore facing Galilee.
en.R: They sailed to the land where the Gerasene people lived. It was across the lake from Galilee.

es.L: Y navegaron hasta la región de los gerasenos, que está frente a Galilea.
es.B: Arribaron a la tierra de los gerasenos, en la orilla de enfrente de Galilea.
es.R: Navegaron hasta la tierra donde vivían los gerasenos. Estaba al otro lado del lago, frente a Galilea.

fr.L: Et ils abordèrent dans la région des Géraséniens, qui est en face de la Galilée.
fr.B: Ils accostèrent au pays des Géraséniens, sur la rive qui fait face à la Galilée.
fr.R: Ils sont arrivés en bateau dans le pays où vivaient les Géraséniens. Ce pays se trouvait de l’autre côté du lac, en face de la Galilée.

sw.L: Na wakasafiri kwa mashua mpaka nchi ya Wagerasi, iliyo ng'ambo, kuelekeana na Galilaya.
sw.B: Walitia nanga katika nchi ya Wagerasi, ng'ambo ya ziwa kuelekeana na Galilaya.
sw.R: Walisafiri mpaka nchi walimoishi Wagerasi. Ilikuwa ng'ambo ya ziwa, upande wa pili kutoka Galilaya.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 배를 저어 거라사 사람들의 지방에 이르렀다. 그곳은 갈릴리 맞은편에 있다.
ko.B: 그들은 갈릴리 맞은편에 있는 거라사 사람들의 지방에 배를 대었다.
ko.R: 그들은 배를 타고 거라사 사람들이 사는 땅으로 갔다. 그곳은 갈릴리에서 호수 건너편에 있었다.

vi.L: Và họ đi thuyền đến vùng của người Giê-ra-sê, là vùng đối diện với Ga-li-lê.
vi.B: Họ ghé vào vùng đất của người Giê-ra-sê, ở bờ đối diện với Ga-li-lê.
vi.R: Họ đi thuyền đến vùng đất của người Giê-ra-sê. Vùng ấy ở bên kia hồ, đối diện với miền Ga-li-lê.

decisions.choice: Gerasenes: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Gadarenes, the reading of many manuscripts
Gergesenes, the reading of some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Several early manuscripts read "Gerasenes". Many others, including most later ones, read "Gadarenes", the name found in Matthew 8:28, and some read "Gergesenes". Gerasa and Gadara were Gentile cities southeast of the lake, Gadara much closer to it; Gergesa may have been a town on the eastern shore. A region could be named after a city some distance away. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: opposite Galilee: on the eastern side of the lake, a mostly Gentile area
decisions.reason: This is the first time in Luke that Jesus goes into Gentile territory. The herd of pigs (8:32) fits a Gentile area.

decisions.choice: sailed down: sailed to land from the open water
decisions.reason: The verb is used of coming in from the sea to the shore.

decisions.choice: "거라사 사람들" for the Gerasenes, as in Mark 5:1
decisions.reason: "거라사" is the established Protestant form (style guide, section 5); the Korean Mark says "거라사 사람들".

decisions.choice: "người Giê-ra-sê"
decisions.reason: As in Mark 5:1: the Protestant transliteration of the SBLGNT reading "Gerasenes"; the variant names are in the footnote.

source.text: ἐξελθόντι δὲ αὐτῷ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ὑπήντησεν ἀνήρ τις ἐκ τῆς πόλεως ἔχων δαιμόνια· καὶ χρόνῳ ἱκανῷ οὐκ ἐνεδύσατο ἱμάτιον, καὶ ἐν οἰκίᾳ οὐκ ἔμενεν ἀλλ’ ἐν τοῖς μνήμασιν.

records.literal_gloss: Having gone out then he onto the land, met [him] a man certain out of the city having demons; and [for] time long not he had put on clothing, and in a house not was living but in the tombs.

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had gone out onto the land, a certain man from the city who had demons met [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}]; and for a long time he had not put on clothing, and he was not living in a house but in the tombs.
en.B: As Jesus stepped onto the shore, a man from the town came toward {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He had demons in him, and for a long time he had gone without clothes and had lived, not in a house, but among the tombs.
en.R: When Jesus got out of the boat, a man from the town came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Demons lived in this man. For a long time he had not worn any clothes. He did not live in a house. He lived in the burial caves.

es.L: Y al salir {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a tierra, [{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] salió al encuentro un hombre de la ciudad que tenía demonios; y desde hacía mucho tiempo no se había puesto ropa, y no vivía en una casa, sino en los sepulcros.
es.B: Cuando Jesús bajó a tierra, un hombre del pueblo salió a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} encuentro. Tenía demonios, y desde hacía mucho tiempo andaba sin ropa y no vivía en una casa, sino entre los sepulcros.
es.R: Cuando Jesús salió de la barca, un hombre del pueblo fue a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} encuentro. Este hombre tenía demonios dentro. Hacía mucho tiempo que no se ponía ropa. No vivía en una casa. Vivía en las cuevas donde se enterraba a los muertos.

fr.L: Et quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fut sorti sur la terre ferme, un homme de la ville, qui avait des démons, vint à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} rencontre ; et depuis longtemps il ne portait pas de vêtement, et il ne demeurait pas dans une maison, mais dans les tombeaux.
fr.B: Comme Jésus mettait pied à terre, un homme de la ville vint à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} rencontre. Il avait des démons en lui ; depuis longtemps, il allait sans vêtements et n’habitait pas dans une maison, mais parmi les tombeaux.
fr.R: Quand Jésus est descendu du bateau, un homme de la ville est venu vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Des démons vivaient dans cet homme. Depuis longtemps, il ne portait plus de vêtements. Il n’habitait pas dans une maison. Il vivait dans les grottes où l’on enterrait les morts.

sw.L: Na alipotoka [kwenda] nchi kavu, mtu fulani kutoka mjini mwenye pepo alikutana [{{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}]; na kwa muda mrefu hakuwa amevaa nguo, wala hakuwa akiishi katika nyumba bali makaburini.
sw.B: Yesu alipotoka katika mashua na kukanyaga nchi kavu, mtu mmoja wa mjini alikuja kukutana {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}. Alikuwa na pepo, na kwa muda mrefu alikuwa havai nguo, wala hakuishi nyumbani, bali makaburini.
sw.R: Yesu alipotoka katika mashua, mtu mmoja wa mjini alikuja {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}. Mtu huyo alikuwa na pepo ndani yake. Kwa muda mrefu hakuwa amevaa nguo yoyote. Hakuishi katika nyumba. Aliishi katika mapango ya kuzikia wafu.

ko.L: 그분이 뭍에 내리셨을 때에, 귀신들이 들린 그 고을 출신의 어떤 사람이 [그분을] 맞았다. 그는 오랫동안 옷을 입지 않았고, 집에서 지내지 않고 무덤들 사이에서 지냈다.
ko.B: 예수께서 뭍에 내리시자, 그 고을에서 온 어떤 사람이 예수를 맞으러 나왔다. 그는 귀신들이 들린 사람이었는데, 오랫동안 옷을 입지 않았고, 집에서 살지 않고 무덤들 사이에서 살았다.
ko.R: 예수께서 배에서 내리셨을 때, 그 고을에 살던 한 사람이 예수께 왔다. 그 사람 속에는 귀신들이 들어 있었다. 그는 오랫동안 옷을 입지 않았다. 집에서 살지 않고, 바위를 파서 만든 무덤 동굴에서 살았다.

vi.L: Và khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bước lên đất, có một người từ trong thành ra gặp [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}], là người có các quỷ; đã lâu rồi anh ta không mặc áo, và không ở trong nhà, nhưng ở giữa các mộ.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu vừa bước lên bờ thì có một người trong thị trấn ra gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Người này bị quỷ ám, đã lâu không mặc quần áo, và không ở trong nhà mà ở giữa các mộ.
vi.R: Khi Đức Giê-xu ra khỏi thuyền, có một người trong thị trấn đến gặp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Người này bị nhiều quỷ ám. Đã lâu anh ta không mặc quần áo. Anh ta không ở trong nhà mà ở trong các hang mộ.

decisions.choice: the tombs: burial places cut into rock outside a town
decisions.reason: Tombs were often caves or rooms cut in the rock. Touching the dead or a grave made a person unclean under the law (Numbers 19:11-16), so living among them cut the man off from other people.

decisions.choice: having demons: under the control of demons
decisions.reason: Luke uses the same way of speaking at 4:33. In 8:30 it becomes clear that there were many.

decisions.choice: the city: the town of that region, where the man had lived
decisions.reason: The man came from the town and later goes back to tell its people what Jesus did (8:39).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of the story.

decisions.choice: the burial caves
decisions.reason: Readable describes the kind of tombs, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: la ciudad (L); el pueblo (B, R)
decisions.reason: The place was the town of that region (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps "ciudad" for the Greek word; Balanced and Readable say "pueblo", since "ciudad" suggests a city, as in Mark 5:14. The same in verses 34 and 39.

decisions.choice: los sepulcros (L, B); las cuevas donde se enterraba a los muertos (R)
decisions.reason: These were burial places cut into the rock (meaning decision m1), and the English Readable says "burial caves", so Readable says so too, as in Mark 5:2.

decisions.choice: vint à sa rencontre, without brackets
decisions.reason: English Literal brackets the object "[him]" of "met". French renders the verb with "venir à la rencontre de", whose complement is part of the expression, as in Mark 5:2, so nothing is bracketed.

decisions.choice: pepo (every level)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet word for a demon, recorded once in this chapter; "Shetani" is kept for Satan himself.

decisions.choice: makaburini (L, B); mapango ya kuzikia wafu (R)
decisions.reason: These were burial places cut into the rock (meaning decision m1), and the English Readable says "burial caves", so Readable says so too, as in Mark 5:2.

decisions.choice: "귀신" for daimonion, "귀신 들린" for "having demons"; "무덤들" (L, B), "바위를 파서 만든 무덤 동굴" (R)
decisions.reason: "귀신" is the word for daimonion in the Korean Mark and Luke 4. Readable describes the tombs as the meaning decision does, close to the Korean Mark 5:2 "무덤 동굴".

decisions.choice: "anh ta" for the man; "thành" (L), "thị trấn" (B, R) for the town (also 8:34, 8:39)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 5:2: "anh ta" is neutral for a man of unknown age; "hắn" would make the narrator despise him. The words for the town follow Luke 4:29.

source.text: ἰδὼν δὲ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀνακράξας προσέπεσεν αὐτῷ καὶ φωνῇ μεγάλῃ εἶπεν· Τί ἐμοὶ καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ υἱὲ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ὑψίστου;

records.literal_gloss: Having seen then Jesus, having cried out he fell down before him and in a voice loud said: What to me and to you, Jesus, Son of God the Most High?

en.L: And seeing Jesus, he cried out and fell down before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and with a loud voice he said, "What [is there] between me and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Jesus, Son of the Most High God?
en.B: When the man saw Jesus, he screamed and threw himself down before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. In a loud voice he said, "What business do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God?
en.R: When the man saw Jesus, he screamed and fell down in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He shouted, "Jesus, Son of the Most High God, why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bothering me?

es.B: Cuando vio a Jesús, dio un alarido, se postró delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y gritó con fuerza: «¿Qué tienes que ver conmigo, Jesús, Hijo del Dios Altísimo?
es.R: Cuando el hombre vio a Jesús, gritó y cayó al suelo delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Gritó: «Jesús, Hijo del Dios Altísimo, ¿por qué me molestas?

fr.L: Et voyant Jésus, il poussa un cri, se jeta devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et d’une voix forte il dit : « Qu’[y a-t-il] entre moi et {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, Jésus, Fils du Dieu Très-Haut ?
fr.B: Quand l’homme vit Jésus, il poussa un grand cri et se jeta à terre devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. D’une voix forte, il dit : « Qu’as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} à faire avec moi, Jésus, Fils du Dieu Très-Haut ?
fr.R: Quand l’homme a vu Jésus, il a crié et il est tombé devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Il a hurlé : « Jésus, Fils du Dieu Très-Haut, pourquoi viens-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} me déranger ?

sw.B: Alipomwona Yesu, alipiga yowe, akajitupa chini mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, akasema kwa sauti kubwa, "Una shughuli gani nami, Yesu, Mwana wa Mungu Aliye Juu Kabisa?
sw.R: Yule mtu alipomwona Yesu, alipiga kelele, akaanguka chini mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Alipaza sauti, "Yesu, Mwana wa Mungu Aliye Juu Kabisa, kwa nini unanisumbua?

ko.L: 그런데 그는 예수를 보자 소리를 지르며 그분 앞에 엎드려 큰 소리로 말했다. "나와 당신 사이에 무슨 [상관이 있습니까], 지극히 높으신 하나님의 아들 예수여?
ko.B: 그는 예수를 보자 소리를 지르며 그 앞에 엎드렸다. 그리고 큰 소리로 말했다. "지극히 높으신 하나님의 아들 예수여, 당신이 나에게 무슨 볼일이 있습니까?
ko.R: 그 사람은 예수를 보자 소리를 지르며 예수 앞에 엎드렸다. 그리고 큰 소리로 외쳤다. "지극히 높으신 하나님의 아들 예수여, 왜 나를 가만두지 않습니까?

vi.L: Khi thấy Đức Giê-xu, anh ta kêu lên, sấp mình trước {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và nói lớn tiếng: "[Có việc] gì giữa tôi với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, hỡi Đức Giê-xu, Con Đức Chúa Trời Chí Cao?
vi.B: Thấy Đức Giê-xu, anh ta thét lên, sấp mình xuống trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và nói lớn: "Hỡi Đức Giê-xu, Con Đức Chúa Trời Chí Cao, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} muốn gì với tôi?
vi.R: Khi thấy Đức Giê-xu, anh ta thét lên và quỳ xuống trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Anh ta la lớn: "Hỡi Đức Giê-xu, Con Đức Chúa Trời Chí Cao! Sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại đến quấy rầy tôi?

decisions.choice: what is there between me and you: what do you have to do with me; leave me alone
alternatives: what do we have in common
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used at 4:34. In the Old Testament it rejects someone's interference (Judges 11:12; 1 Kings 17:18).

decisions.choice: Son of the Most High God: the demon knows who Jesus is
decisions.reason: Gabriel said that Jesus would be called Son of the Most High (1:32), and demons have already cried out that he is the Son of God (4:34, 41). "Most High God" is a title for God used in Scripture, often on the lips of non-Israelites (Genesis 14:18-20; Daniel 3:26; Acts 16:17).

decisions.choice: he cried out ... me: the man speaks, but the words come from the demons
decisions.reason: The voice is the man's, but what he says is what the demons fear (8:30-31).

decisions.choice: Jesus, Son of the Most High God, why are you bothering me?
alternatives: What is there between me and you?
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means, as at 4:34, and puts the name first.

decisions.choice: ¿Qué [hay] para mí y para ti?
decisions.reason: The Greek idiom says "what to me and to you" (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps its two datives in their order, as in Mark 5:7, so the separate pronoun "ti" can carry the setting; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: Mungu Aliye Juu Kabisa
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering of "the Most High". The Greek is a superlative; "Aliye Juu Kabisa" (who is highest of all) says that, as in Mark 5:7.

decisions.choice: The demon speaks through the man to Jesus in 합쇼체 with "당신", no honorific -시- or "께" for him, and of itself as "나"
decisions.reason: As settled for the Korean Gospels (Mark 5:7, Luke 4:34): the spirit bows and names Jesus truly, so it speaks up to him in formal endings, while "당신" keeps its distance.

decisions.choice: "당신이 나에게 무슨 볼일이 있습니까?" (B); "왜 나를 가만두지 않습니까?" (R), as in Mark 5:7
decisions.reason: The synoptic parallel reads alike in Korean; the idiom means "leave me alone" (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "tôi" and "Ngài" (with the setting) in the man's words
decisions.reason: As in the parallel Mark 5:7 and in Luke 4:41: the spirit speaking through the man names Jesus as the Son of the Most High God (meaning decision), so Vietnamese gives him the reverent "Ngài" for "you", where the hostile demon of 4:34 says "ông".

source.text: δέομαί σου, μή με βασανίσῃς·

en.L: I beg {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, do not torment me."
en.B: I beg {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, do not torment me!"
en.R: I beg {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, do not make me suffer!"

es.L: Te ruego, no me atormentes».
es.B: ¡Te suplico que no me tortures!».
es.R: ¡Te ruego que no me hagas sufrir!».

fr.L: Je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} prie, ne me tourmente pas. »

fr.R: Je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}en supplie, ne me fais pas souffrir ! »

sw.R: Nakuomba, usinifanye niteseke!"

vi.R: Tôi van xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, đừng làm khổ tôi!"

decisions.choice: torment: torture or punish
decisions.reason: The verb means to torture. The demons fear the punishment that awaits them (Matthew 8:29; Revelation 20:10).

decisions.choice: make me suffer
decisions.reason: Readable uses simpler words.

decisions.choice: Te, with no span
decisions.reason: The English "you" takes the setting. In Spanish the pronoun begins the sentence and is capitalised either way, so a span would have nothing to change.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on nakusihi, nakuomba (I beg you)
decisions.reason: The English "you" takes the setting. Swahili carries it in the object prefix -ku- of the verb, which cannot take a capital, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

source.text: παρήγγελλεν γὰρ τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἀκαθάρτῳ ἐξελθεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.

records.literal_gloss: He was commanding for the spirit the unclean to come out from the man.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was commanding the unclean spirit to come out of the man.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been ordering the unclean spirit to leave the man.
en.R: The man said this because Jesus had been telling the evil spirit to come out of him.

es.L: Porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mandaba al espíritu impuro que saliera del hombre.
es.B: Es que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} había estado ordenando al espíritu impuro que saliera del hombre.
es.R: El hombre dijo esto porque Jesús le había estado ordenando al espíritu maligno que saliera de él.

fr.L: Car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ordonnait à l’esprit impur de sortir de l’homme.
fr.B: En effet, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait ordonné à l’esprit impur de quitter cet homme.
fr.R: L’homme a dit cela parce que Jésus avait ordonné à l’esprit mauvais de sortir de lui.

sw.L: Kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alikuwa akimwamuru pepo mchafu amtoke mtu huyo.
sw.B: Kwa kuwa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alikuwa amekwisha kumwamuru yule pepo mchafu amtoke mtu huyo.
sw.R: Mtu huyo alisema hivyo kwa sababu Yesu alikuwa akimwamuru yule pepo mbaya amtoke.

ko.L: 그분이 더러운 영에게 그 사람에게서 나가라고 명령하고 계셨기 때문이다.
ko.B: 예수께서 더러운 영에게 그 사람에게서 나가라고 명령하고 계셨던 것이다.
ko.R: 그 사람이 이렇게 말한 것은, 예수께서 이미 악한 영에게 그 사람에게서 나가라고 말씀하고 계셨기 때문이다.

vi.L: Vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang truyền cho linh ô uế ra khỏi người ấy.
vi.B: Ấy là vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã ra lệnh cho linh ô uế phải ra khỏi người ấy.
vi.R: Anh ta nói vậy vì Đức Giê-xu đã ra lệnh cho tà linh ra khỏi anh ta.

decisions.choice: for he was commanding: the reason for the cry in 8:28
alternatives: a new command given after the cry
decisions.reason: Luke explains after the event why the demon cried out: Jesus had already begun to order it out (as Mark 5:8).

decisions.choice: the unclean spirit: the demon
decisions.reason: Luke uses "unclean spirit" and "demon" for the same thing (4:33, 35; 8:27).

decisions.choice: evil spirit
decisions.reason: Readable's usual word, as at 4:33, since young readers would take "unclean" to mean dirty.

decisions.choice: The man said this because
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "for" explains.

decisions.choice: espíritu impuro (L, B); espíritu maligno (R)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering, recorded once in this chapter. "Inmundo" now sounds like dirt; "impuro" says the spirit makes a person unfit to come near God, and Readable says plainly that it is evil, as the English does.

decisions.choice: l’esprit impur (L, B); l’esprit mauvais (R)
decisions.reason: "Un esprit impur" is the term set for the New Testament (style guide section 9). Readable follows the English "evil spirit", as Mark 5 does, since young readers would take "impur" to mean dirty.

decisions.choice: pepo mchafu (L, B); pepo mbaya (R)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering, recorded once in this chapter. "Roho" is kept for the human spirit and the Spirit of God (as in verse 55); Readable says plainly that the spirit is evil, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "더러운 영" (L, B); "악한 영" (R), as in Mark 5:8 and Luke 4:36
alternatives: "악한 영" at every level, as in 8:2
decisions.reason: Luke here says "unclean", so Literal and Balanced keep Mark's word; Readable uses the plainer word, as the English Readable says "evil spirit".

decisions.choice: "linh ô uế" (L, B); "tà linh" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled terms for the unclean spirits in the Gospels, as in Mark 5:2 and Luke 4:36.

source.text: πολλοῖς γὰρ χρόνοις συνηρπάκει αὐτόν, καὶ ἐδεσμεύετο ἁλύσεσιν καὶ πέδαις φυλασσόμενος, καὶ διαρρήσσων τὰ δεσμὰ ἠλαύνετο ὑπὸ τοῦ δαιμονίου εἰς τὰς ἐρήμους.

records.literal_gloss: Many for times it had seized him, and he was bound with chains and shackles being guarded, and breaking the bonds he was driven by the demon into the deserted [places].

en.L: For many times it had seized him, and he was bound with chains and shackles, being kept under guard, and breaking the bonds, he was driven by the demon into the deserted places.
en.B: Again and again it had taken hold of him. People kept him under guard and bound him with chains and fetters, but he would break the bonds, and the demon would drive him out into the wilderness.
en.R: The demon had taken control of him many times. People had tried to keep him under guard, tied up with chains on his hands and feet. But he would break the chains, and the demon would drive him out into lonely places where no one lived.

es.L: Porque muchas veces se había apoderado de él, y era atado con cadenas y grilletes, estando bajo custodia, y rompiendo las ataduras, era arrastrado por el demonio a los lugares desiertos.
es.B: Muchas veces se había apoderado de él. Lo tenían bajo vigilancia y lo ataban con cadenas y grilletes, pero él rompía las ataduras, y el demonio lo arrastraba al desierto.
es.R: El demonio se había apoderado de él muchas veces. La gente había tratado de tenerlo vigilado, atado con cadenas en las manos y en los pies. Pero él rompía las cadenas, y el demonio lo llevaba a lugares solitarios donde no vivía nadie.

fr.L: Car bien des fois il s’était emparé de lui, et il était lié de chaînes et d’entraves, gardé à vue, et, rompant les liens, il était poussé par le démon dans les lieux déserts.
fr.B: Bien des fois, le démon s’était emparé de lui. On le gardait enchaîné, les fers aux pieds, mais il brisait ses liens, et le démon l’entraînait au désert.
fr.R: Le démon avait pris le contrôle de cet homme beaucoup de fois. Les gens avaient essayé de le surveiller. Ils lui avaient mis des chaînes aux mains et aux pieds. Mais il cassait les chaînes, et le démon le poussait vers des endroits déserts où personne n’habitait.

sw.L: Kwa maana mara nyingi alikuwa amemkamata, naye alikuwa akifungwa kwa minyororo na pingu, akilindwa, na akivunja vifungo, alikuwa akiswagwa na yule pepo kwenda nyikani.
sw.B: Mara nyingi pepo huyo alikuwa amemshika. Watu walimweka chini ya ulinzi na kumfunga kwa minyororo na pingu, lakini yeye alivunja vifungo hivyo, na pepo akamswaga mpaka nyikani.
sw.R: Pepo huyo alikuwa amemtawala mara nyingi. Watu walijaribu kumlinda, wakamfunga minyororo mikononi na miguuni. Lakini alivunja minyororo hiyo, na pepo akampeleka mahali pasipo na watu.

ko.L: 그것이 여러 번 그를 사로잡았기 때문이다. 그는 감시를 받으며 쇠사슬과 족쇄에 묶여 있었으나, 그 묶은 것들을 끊고 귀신에게 몰려 광야로 가곤 했다.
ko.B: 귀신은 여러 번 그를 사로잡았다. 사람들이 그를 감시하며 쇠사슬과 족쇄로 묶어 두었지만, 그는 묶인 것을 끊어 버렸고, 귀신은 그를 광야로 몰아내곤 했다.
ko.R: 귀신은 여러 번 그 사람을 사로잡았다. 사람들은 그를 지키면서 그의 손과 발을 쇠사슬로 묶어 두려고 했다. 그러나 그는 그때마다 쇠사슬을 끊어 버렸다. 그러면 귀신은 그를 아무도 살지 않는 외딴 곳으로 몰아냈다.

vi.L: Vì đã nhiều lần nó bắt giữ anh ta, và anh ta bị trói bằng xích và cùm, bị canh giữ, nhưng anh ta bứt đứt các dây trói và bị quỷ đuổi vào những nơi hoang vắng.
vi.B: Đã nhiều lần nó chiếm lấy anh ta. Người ta canh giữ anh ta, lấy xích và cùm trói anh ta lại, nhưng anh ta bứt đứt dây trói, và quỷ đuổi anh ta vào nơi hoang vắng.
vi.R: Tà linh đã nhiều lần chiếm lấy anh ta. Người ta đã cố canh giữ anh ta, lấy xích trói tay và cùm chân anh ta. Nhưng anh ta bứt đứt xích, và quỷ đuổi anh ta vào những nơi vắng vẻ, không có người ở.

decisions.choice: many times: again and again
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "for a long time" or "many times". "It had seized him" suggests repeated attacks. Either way the man had suffered for years.

decisions.choice: chains and shackles: chains, and fetters for the feet
decisions.reason: The second word means fetters for the feet. He was bound hand and foot.

decisions.choice: the deserted places: the wilderness, where no one lived
decisions.reason: The word means empty, lonely land. Such places were thought of as the haunts of evil spirits (11:24).

decisions.choice: People
alternatives: he was bound ... being kept under guard
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply who bound and guarded him, so that the sentence can be active.

decisions.choice: "귀신은" as the subject (B, R); "그것이" (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the subject in the verb; Korean names it, and Luke names the demon in the same sentence.

decisions.choice: "족쇄" for the fetters, as in Mark 5:4; "광야" (L, B), "아무도 살지 않는 외딴 곳" (R)
decisions.reason: "족쇄" is the everyday word; "광야" is the established word for the uninhabited places, which Readable describes (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "nó" for the spirit
decisions.reason: As in Luke 4:35 and Mark 1:25: the narrator speaks of a demon or spirit as "nó"; "hắn" is kept for the devil.

en.B: Jesus asked him, "What is your name?"
en.R: Jesus asked him, "What is your name?"

es.B: Jesús le preguntó: «¿Cómo te llamas?».
es.R: Jesús le preguntó: «¿Cómo te llamas?».

fr.B: Jésus lui demanda : « Quel est ton nom ? »
fr.R: Jésus lui a demandé : « Comment t’appelles-tu ? »

ko.R: 예수께서 그에게 물으셨다. "네 이름이 무엇이냐?"

vi.R: Đức Giê-xu hỏi anh ta: "Anh tên gì?"

decisions.choice: him, your: Jesus speaks to the man, and the demons answer through him
alternatives: Jesus speaks to one demon only
decisions.reason: The answer in 8:30 shows that many demons were speaking.

decisions.choice: Jesus says "anh" to the man
decisions.reason: As in Mark 5:9: the question is put to the man (meaning decision), and "anh" is the ordinary respectful word for a grown man.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Λεγιών, ὅτι εἰσῆλθεν δαιμόνια πολλὰ εἰς αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And he said: Legion, because entered demons many into him.

en.L: And he said, "Legion," because many demons had entered into him.
en.B: He said, "Legion"; for a great number of demons had entered him.
en.R: He answered, "My name is Legion." A legion was a group of thousands of soldiers. He said this because many demons had gone into him.

es.L: Y él dijo: «Legión», porque muchos demonios habían entrado en él.
es.B: Él respondió: «Legión», porque eran muchos los demonios que habían entrado en él.
es.R: Él contestó: «Me llamo Legión». Una legión era un grupo de miles de soldados. Dijo esto porque muchos demonios habían entrado en él.

fr.L: Et il dit : « Légion », parce que beaucoup de démons étaient entrés en lui.
fr.B: « Légion », répondit-il ; car de nombreux démons étaient entrés en lui.
fr.R: Il a répondu : « Je m’appelle Légion. » Une légion, c’était un groupe de plusieurs milliers de soldats. Il a dit cela parce que beaucoup de démons étaient entrés en lui.

sw.L: Naye akasema, "Legioni," kwa sababu pepo wengi walikuwa wamemwingia.
sw.B: Akajibu, "Legioni," kwa maana pepo wengi sana walikuwa wamemwingia.
sw.R: Akajibu, "Naitwa Legioni." Legioni kilikuwa kikosi cha maelfu ya askari. Alisema hivyo kwa sababu pepo wengi walikuwa wamemwingia.

ko.L: 그가 말했다. "레기온입니다." 많은 귀신이 그에게 들어갔기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그가 "레기온입니다" 하고 대답했다. 많은 귀신이 그 사람 속에 들어가 있었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그가 대답했다. "내 이름은 레기온입니다." 레기온은 수천 명의 군인으로 이루어진 로마 군대의 부대를 가리키는 말이었다. 그가 이렇게 대답한 것은 많은 귀신이 그 사람 속에 들어가 있었기 때문이다.

vi.L: Anh ta nói: "Quân Đoàn"; vì nhiều quỷ đã nhập vào anh ta.
vi.B: Anh ta đáp: "Quân Đoàn"; vì có rất nhiều quỷ đã nhập vào anh ta.
vi.R: Anh ta trả lời: "Tên tôi là Quân Đoàn." Quân đoàn là một đơn vị quân đội có hàng nghìn binh lính. Anh ta nói vậy vì có rất nhiều quỷ đã nhập vào anh ta.

decisions.choice: Legion: a unit of the Roman army, several thousand soldiers
decisions.reason: A full legion had about 6,000 soldiers. The name says that a great army of demons held the man.

decisions.choice: because many demons had entered him: Luke's explanation
decisions.reason: These words are the narrator's, explaining the name.

decisions.choice: My name is ... A legion was a group of thousands of soldiers.
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name.

decisions.choice: Legioni
decisions.reason: Legion is used as a name, taken from the Roman army unit of several thousand soldiers (meaning decision m1). "Jeshi" (army) would turn the name into an ordinary word; "Legioni" keeps it a name, as in Mark 5:9, and Readable explains it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "레기온" at every level, explained at Readable
decisions.reason: As in Mark 5:9 in Korean, the Latin word stays a name; "군대" alone would hide that it is a Roman unit. Readable explains it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "Quân Đoàn", capitalised as a name
decisions.reason: As in Mark 5:9: "quân đoàn" is the Vietnamese word for a large army unit, the sense of the Roman word (meaning decision).

source.text: καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν ἵνα μὴ ἐπιτάξῃ αὐτοῖς εἰς τὴν ἄβυσσον ἀπελθεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: And they were begging him that not he would command them into the abyss to go away.

en.L: And they were begging {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would not command them to go away into the abyss.
en.B: The demons kept pleading with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} not to command them to depart into the abyss.
en.R: The demons kept begging Jesus not to send them into the bottomless pit where evil spirits are kept.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suplicaban que no les ordenara irse al abismo.
es.B: Los demonios {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rogaban una y otra vez que no les mandara ir al abismo.
es.R: Los demonios le rogaban a Jesús que no los enviara al pozo sin fondo donde se encierra a los espíritus malignos.

fr.L: Et ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suppliaient de ne pas leur ordonner de s’en aller dans l’abîme.
fr.B: Les démons {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suppliaient de ne pas leur ordonner de partir dans l’abîme.
fr.R: Les démons suppliaient Jésus de ne pas les envoyer dans le gouffre sans fond où l’on enferme les esprits mauvais.

sw.L: Nao walikuwa wakimsihi asiwaamuru kwenda zao kilindini.
sw.B: Pepo hao waliendelea kumsihi asiwaamuru waende kilindini.
sw.R: Pepo hao walimsihi Yesu asiwapeleke katika shimo lisilo na mwisho, ambamo pepo wabaya hufungwa.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 자기들에게 깊은 구렁으로 가라고 명령하지 말아 달라고 그분께 간청하고 있었다.
ko.B: 귀신들은 자기들을 깊은 구렁으로 들어가라고 명령하지 말아 달라고 예수께 거듭 애원했다.
ko.R: 귀신들은 예수께 자기들을 깊은 구덩이로 보내지 말아 달라고 계속 빌었다. 그곳은 악한 영들을 가두어 두는 곳이었다.

vi.L: Và chúng nài xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đừng truyền cho chúng đi vào vực sâu.
vi.B: Các quỷ cứ van nài {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đừng ra lệnh cho chúng xuống vực sâu.
vi.R: Các quỷ cứ van xin Đức Giê-xu đừng đuổi chúng xuống vực sâu không đáy, là nơi giam giữ các tà linh.

decisions.choice: the abyss: the deep place where evil spirits are held for judgment
decisions.reason: The word means a bottomless depth. In Revelation it is the prison of evil powers (Revelation 9:1-2, 11; 20:1-3). Romans 10:7 uses it of the realm of the dead.

decisions.choice: they were begging: the demons, many of them, kept pleading
decisions.reason: The verb is plural and continuous. After the name Legion, the demons speak as a group.

decisions.choice: The demons
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who was begging.

decisions.choice: the bottomless pit where evil spirits are kept
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word, as the meaning decision does.

decisions.choice: el abismo (L, B); el pozo sin fondo donde se encierra a los espíritus malignos (R)
decisions.reason: The deep place where evil spirits are held for judgment (meaning decision m1). "Abismo" is the word of Romans 10:7 and keeps the Greek picture; Readable explains it, as the English Readable does. "Hades" is kept for the place of the dead.

decisions.choice: kilindi (L, B); shimo lisilo na mwisho (R)
decisions.reason: The deep place where evil spirits are held for judgment (meaning decision m1). The term sheet keeps "Kuzimu" for Hades, the place of the dead, so this uses "kilindi" (the deep); Readable explains it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "깊은 구렁" (L, B); "악한 영들을 가두어 두는 깊은 구덩이" (R) for abyssos
decisions.reason: "무저갱" is the older church word of familiar versions and is not current Korean; "깊은 구렁" says a deep pit plainly. Readable says what the place is for (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "귀신들은" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Korean names who is begging, as the English Balanced and Readable do (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "vực sâu" (L, B); "vực sâu không đáy, là nơi giam giữ các tà linh" (R)
decisions.reason: "Vực sâu" is the plain word for the deep place; "âm phủ" is the world of the dead and would say something else. Readable explains it, as the English Readable does (meaning decision).

source.text: Ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ ἀγέλη χοίρων ἱκανῶν βοσκομένη ἐν τῷ ὄρει· καὶ παρεκάλεσαν αὐτὸν ἵνα ἐπιτρέψῃ αὐτοῖς εἰς ἐκείνους εἰσελθεῖν· καὶ ἐπέτρεψεν αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: There was then there a herd of pigs many feeding on the mountain; and they begged him that he would allow them into those to enter; and he allowed them.

en.L: Now there was there a herd of many pigs feeding on the mountain; and they begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would allow them to enter into those; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} allowed them.
en.B: Now a large herd of pigs was feeding there on the mountainside. The demons begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for permission to enter those pigs, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} allowed them to.
en.R: Many pigs were eating on the hill nearby. The demons begged Jesus to let them go into the pigs. Jesus let them do it.

es.L: Y había allí una piara de muchos cerdos paciendo en el monte; y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rogaron que les permitiera entrar en aquellos; y se lo permitió.
es.B: Había allí una gran piara de cerdos paciendo en la ladera del monte. Los demonios {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suplicaron que les permitiera entrar en los cerdos, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se lo permitió.
es.R: En el cerro cercano había muchos cerdos comiendo. Los demonios le rogaron a Jesús que los dejara entrar en los cerdos. Jesús los dejó.

fr.L: Or il y avait là un troupeau de nombreux porcs qui paissait sur la montagne ; et ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} supplièrent de leur permettre d’entrer dans ceux-là ; et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le leur permit.
fr.B: Or un grand troupeau de porcs paissait là, sur le flanc de la montagne. Les démons {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} supplièrent de les laisser entrer dans ces porcs, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le leur permit.
fr.R: Tout près, sur la colline, beaucoup de cochons mangeaient. Les démons ont supplié Jésus de les laisser entrer dans les cochons. Jésus leur a permis de le faire.

sw.L: Basi palikuwa na kundi la nguruwe wengi pale likila malisho mlimani; nao wakamsihi awaruhusu kuwaingia hao; naye akawaruhusu.
sw.B: Pale kulikuwa na kundi kubwa la nguruwe likila malisho kwenye mteremko wa mlima. Pepo hao walimsihi awaruhusu kuwaingia nguruwe hao, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akawaruhusu.
sw.R: Kwenye kilima kilichokuwa karibu, kundi kubwa la nguruwe lilikuwa likila. Pepo walimsihi Yesu awaruhusu kuwaingia nguruwe hao. Yesu akawaruhusu.

ko.L: 그런데 거기 산에는 많은 돼지 떼가 먹이를 먹고 있었다. 그래서 그들은 저 [돼지들] 속으로 들어가게 허락해 달라고 그분께 간청했다. 그러자 그분이 그들에게 허락하셨다.
ko.B: 마침 그곳 산비탈에서 큰 돼지 떼가 먹이를 먹고 있었다. 귀신들은 그 돼지들 속으로 들어가게 해 달라고 예수께 간청했다. 예수께서 그렇게 하도록 허락하셨다.
ko.R: 가까운 산비탈에서 많은 돼지가 먹이를 먹고 있었다. 귀신들은 돼지들 속으로 들어가게 해 달라고 예수께 빌었다. 예수께서 그렇게 하라고 하셨다.

vi.L: Bấy giờ ở đó có một bầy heo đông đang ăn trên núi; và chúng nài xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho phép chúng nhập vào những con ấy; và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho phép chúng.
vi.B: Lúc ấy có một bầy heo rất lớn đang ăn trên sườn núi. Các quỷ nài xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho chúng nhập vào bầy heo ấy, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho phép.
vi.R: Gần đó có một bầy heo rất đông đang ăn trên đồi. Các quỷ van xin Đức Giê-xu cho chúng nhập vào bầy heo. Đức Giê-xu cho phép chúng.

decisions.choice: pigs: unclean animals under the law
decisions.reason: The law forbade Israel to eat pork (Leviticus 11:7; Deuteronomy 14:8). A large herd shows that this was a Gentile area.

decisions.choice: the mountain: the hill country above the lake
decisions.reason: The word can mean hill country. The herd was on the slopes that run down to the water (8:33).

decisions.choice: they begged: the demons
decisions.reason: The subject is the same as in 8:31.

decisions.choice: The demons
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who was begging.

decisions.choice: des porcs (L, B); des cochons (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 5: "porc" is the usual word in careful writing; "cochon" is the everyday word a child knows, so Readable uses it through the story.

decisions.choice: "저 [돼지들]" (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "those"; Korean needs the noun after the demonstrative, so Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: "heo"
decisions.reason: As in Mark 5:11: "heo" (southern) and "lợn" (northern) are both standard; "heo" is the word most Protestant readers know from this story.

source.text: ἐξελθόντα δὲ τὰ δαιμόνια ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἰσῆλθον εἰς τοὺς χοίρους, καὶ ὥρμησεν ἡ ἀγέλη κατὰ τοῦ κρημνοῦ εἰς τὴν λίμνην καὶ ἀπεπνίγη.

records.literal_gloss: Having gone out then the demons from the man they entered into the pigs, and rushed the herd down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.

en.L: And the demons, having come out of the man, entered into the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.
en.B: The demons left the man and went into the pigs. Then the whole herd stampeded down the cliff into the lake and drowned.
en.R: So the demons came out of the man and went into the pigs. Then all the pigs ran down the steep hill into the lake and drowned.

es.L: Y saliendo los demonios del hombre, entraron en los cerdos, y la piara se lanzó por el despeñadero al lago y se ahogó.
es.B: Los demonios salieron del hombre y entraron en los cerdos. Entonces toda la piara se precipitó por el barranco hasta el lago y se ahogó.
es.R: Así que los demonios salieron del hombre y entraron en los cerdos. Entonces todos los cerdos corrieron cuesta abajo por la ladera empinada hasta el lago, y se ahogaron.

fr.L: Et les démons, étant sortis de l’homme, entrèrent dans les porcs, et le troupeau se précipita du haut de l’escarpement dans le lac et se noya.
fr.B: Les démons sortirent de l’homme et entrèrent dans les porcs. Tout le troupeau dévala alors la falaise jusque dans le lac et s’y noya.
fr.R: Alors les démons sont sortis de l’homme et ils sont entrés dans les cochons. Tous les cochons ont couru en bas de la colline très raide, jusque dans le lac, et ils se sont noyés.

sw.L: Na pepo, wakiisha kumtoka mtu huyo, wakawaingia nguruwe, na kundi likatimua mbio kuteremka genge kuingia ziwani, likazama.
sw.B: Pepo walimtoka mtu huyo, wakawaingia nguruwe. Kisha kundi zima likatimua mbio kuteremka genge hadi ziwani, likazama.
sw.R: Basi pepo walimtoka yule mtu, wakawaingia nguruwe. Kisha nguruwe wote walikimbia kuteremka kilima kikali hadi ziwani, wakazama.

ko.L: 그리하여 귀신들이 그 사람에게서 나와 돼지들 속으로 들어갔다. 그러자 그 떼가 비탈 아래로 내달려 호수로 들어가 빠져 죽었다.
ko.B: 귀신들이 그 사람에게서 나와 돼지들 속으로 들어갔다. 그러자 돼지 떼가 가파른 비탈을 내리달려 호수에 뛰어들어 빠져 죽었다.
ko.R: 그래서 귀신들이 그 사람에게서 나와 돼지들 속으로 들어갔다. 그러자 돼지들이 모두 가파른 산비탈을 달려 내려가 호수에 뛰어들었다. 돼지들은 모두 물에 빠져 죽었다.

vi.L: Và các quỷ ra khỏi người ấy, nhập vào bầy heo, và cả bầy lao xuống dốc đứng, xuống hồ, và chết đuối.
vi.B: Các quỷ ra khỏi người ấy và nhập vào bầy heo. Cả bầy lao xuống dốc đứng, nhào xuống hồ và chết đuối.
vi.R: Vậy các quỷ ra khỏi người ấy và nhập vào bầy heo. Rồi cả bầy heo chạy ào xuống sườn đồi dốc đứng, lao xuống hồ và chết đuối hết.

decisions.choice: the steep bank: a cliff or steep slope
decisions.reason: The word means a steep drop. The pigs ran down it straight into the water.

decisions.choice: was drowned: choked by the water
decisions.reason: It is the same verb as "choked" in 8:7. The demons destroy what they enter.

source.text: Ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ βόσκοντες τὸ γεγονὸς ἔφυγον καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ εἰς τοὺς ἀγρούς.

records.literal_gloss: Having seen then those feeding [them] the [thing] having happened, they fled and reported [it] in the city and in the fields.

en.L: And when those who were feeding [them] saw what had happened, they fled and reported [it] in the city and in the fields.
en.B: When the herders saw what had happened, they ran off and spread the news in the town and on the farms.
en.R: Those who took care of the pigs saw what happened. They ran away and told people in the town and in the countryside.

es.L: Y al ver lo que había sucedido, los que [los] apacentaban huyeron y [lo] contaron en la ciudad y en los campos.
es.B: Cuando los que cuidaban los cerdos vieron lo que había pasado, salieron corriendo y dieron la noticia en el pueblo y en los campos.
es.R: Los que cuidaban los cerdos vieron lo que pasó. Huyeron y se lo contaron a la gente en el pueblo y en el campo.

fr.L: Et ceux qui [les] faisaient paître, voyant ce qui était arrivé, s’enfuirent et [le] rapportèrent dans la ville et dans les campagnes.
fr.B: Quand les gardiens du troupeau virent ce qui s’était passé, ils s’enfuirent et portèrent la nouvelle à la ville et dans les fermes des environs.
fr.R: Les hommes qui gardaient les cochons ont vu ce qui s’était passé. Ils se sont enfuis et ils l’ont raconté aux gens de la ville et de la campagne.
